plain_summary: Cash remains important, especially outside major cities. ATMs accepting U.S.-issued cards are available in places such as Montevideo and Punta del Este.

sources.title: Uruguay: U.S. traveler requirements and advisory

title: Card payments and acceptance
plain_summary: Cards are widely used in urban areas but less consistently in rural areas. Keep an alternative and verify the currency and amount on the terminal.

sources.title: Uruguay: U.S. traveler requirements and advisory

title: U.S. advisory and regional risk
plain_summary: Level 2 for crime. Armed robberies and vehicle theft can occur; stay alert around banks, ATMs and poorly lit areas. Do not resist a robbery. Recheck the linked advisory and local alerts before departure.

sources.title: Uruguay: U.S. traveler requirements and advisory

title: Emergency numbers and getting help
plain_summary: Call 911 for police or ambulance help. Give the town and precise address or road location, and contact your insurer after referral for care.

sources.title: Uruguay: U.S. traveler requirements and advisory

title: Identification and local legal precautions
plain_summary: Tourists cannot use the resident cannabis-purchase/growing system. Smoking, including e-cigarettes, is banned in enclosed public places such as restaurants and shopping centers.

sources.title: Uruguay: local conditions, laws and transport safety

title: Weather and outdoor hazards
plain_summary: Heavy storms can cause flooding and disrupt roads. Forest-fire risk increases in hot, dry months. Follow INUMET warnings and local fire restrictions before driving or undertaking outdoor activities.

sources.title: Uruguay: local conditions, laws and transport safety

title: Choosing a taxi or prearranged ride
plain_summary: Carrasco Airport lists transport and travel-service providers in its service directory. Use an identified provider or the information counter to arrange onward travel, confirm the total fare and meeting point, and keep valuables secure while doing so.

sources.title: Services – Carrasco Airport – Montevideo, Uruguay

title: Medical insurance and evacuation cover
plain_summary: Check that your policy covers treatment in Uruguay, existing medical conditions and any planned activities. Include evacuation cover where needed, and keep the assistance number accessible. Contact the insurer promptly if referred for treatment.

sources.title: Uruguay: healthcare and medicines

title: Finding and paying for medical care
plain_summary: Medical and dental treatment can be expensive. Keep funds accessible and obtain insurer assistance. The linked provider list identifies some English-speaking options; specialist medicine may be harder to obtain in small towns.

sources.title: Uruguay: healthcare and medicines

title: Prescription preparation and import checks
plain_summary: Bring enough permitted prescription medicine. Local prescriptions may be needed for replacement supplies; medicines are kept behind pharmacy counters and must be requested. Check import legality before packing.

sources.title: Uruguay: healthcare and medicines

title: Vaccines to discuss before departure
plain_summary: CDC recommends hepatitis A and B vaccination for unvaccinated travelers. Review routine vaccines and measles protection with a clinician before travel; recommendations depend on age, health and itinerary.

sources.title: Uruguay: CDC Traveler View
sources.organization: U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

title: Itinerary-specific health precautions
plain_summary: Prevent mosquito bites and review current CDC notices. Chikungunya vaccination is generally not recommended for ordinary travel on the checked page; discuss individual circumstances and do not infer every traveler needs it.

sources.title: Uruguay: CDC Traveler View
sources.organization: U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

title: Local SIM or eSIM setup
plain_summary: Antel requires mobile-service identification and permits registration with eligible foreign documents. Other document cases need an Antel service location. Check plan, activation/recharge and physical-SIM/eSIM eligibility rather than assuming resident signup requirements fit visitors.

sources.title: ANTEL

title: Arrival controls and travel documents
plain_summary: Uruguay’s migration authority advises carrying a valid travel document and any additional required paperwork, especially minor-travel permissions. Allow time for immigration and the other entry/boarding controls; there is not a blanket exemption because a visit is short.

sources.title: Recomendaciones de Migración para las vacaciones de primavera | MI

title: Carrasco airport buses and regional connections
plain_summary: Carrasco Airport lists independent bus operators for Montevideo, its metropolitan area and regional destinations. Confirm the actual service stop, destination, baggage conditions and schedule with the operator. An airport listing is not a guarantee that every bus serves your hotel.

sources.title: Buses – Carrasco Airport – Montevideo, Uruguay

title: Montevideo STM card for visitors
plain_summary: Montevideo’s STM common card can be obtained at service locations using a passport. Tell staff which journey product you need, check the display, tap the card and keep the issued ticket. Time-based transfers and group use have specific conditions.

sources.title: Tarjeta Común | Portal institucional

title: Check connectivity on the selected coach
plain_summary: Carrasco lists coach operators that advertise onboard Wi-Fi on their services. Verify the actual operator and departure; download essential tickets and accommodation details first rather than relying on connectivity on every bus.

sources.title: Buses – Carrasco Airport – Montevideo, Uruguay

title: Plugs, voltage and device labels
plain_summary: Electrical Safety First lists plug types C/F/L, 220 V and 50 Hz for Uruguay. Check the actual outlet and every device’s input label. A plug adapter changes the fit, not voltage; use only conversion approved for the appliance.

title: Passport validity and travel-document checks
plain_summary: Uzbekistan’s government portal says six months’ passport validity from entry; the U.S. country page says three months beyond the allowed stay and a blank page. Confirm a borderline passport with Uzbek authorities and the airline; the two descriptions should not be silently treated as identical.

title: Short tourist visit: permission and stay limit
plain_summary: From January 1, 2026, U.S. citizens may enter Uzbekistan visa-free for up to 30 days, according to the government’s announcement. Longer stays need the appropriate visa; check that your activity fits the allowed route.

title: Local currency and budgeting
plain_summary: Uzbekistan uses the Uzbekistani sum (UZS). Exchange foreign cash for local currency rather than expecting U.S. dollars to be accepted as payment.

sources.title: Uzbekistan: U.S. traveler requirements and advisory

title: Cash, ATMs and backup payments
plain_summary: ATMs can be scarce outside tourist centers. Arrange enough local cash before regional travel and use official exchange services; black-market exchange is illegal.

sources.title: Uzbekistan: U.S. traveler requirements and advisory

title: Card payments and acceptance
plain_summary: Check card acceptance for each accommodation and service and keep a cash backup. Do not assume remote locations have the same facilities as tourist centers.

sources.title: Uzbekistan: U.S. traveler requirements and advisory

title: U.S. advisory and regional risk
plain_summary: Level 1. Check current official alerts and any route/border restrictions. Be cautious about unsolicited tours and high-priced offers. Recheck the linked advisory and local alerts before departure.

sources.title: Uzbekistan: U.S. traveler requirements and advisory

title: Emergency numbers and getting help
plain_summary: Fire: 101. Police: 102. Ambulance: 103. Tourist police: 1173. Give your precise location; English-speaking medical support may be limited.

sources.title: Uzbekistan: U.S. traveler requirements and advisory

title: Identification and local legal precautions
plain_summary: Carry your passport for identity checks. Ask before photographing government/security sites, airports or border checkpoints; rules and sensitivities vary by location.

title: Weather and outdoor hazards
plain_summary: Uzbekistan is in an active seismic zone and has regular tremors. Learn the accommodation’s emergency instructions and follow local directions after an earthquake; check transport and route conditions before moving into an affected area.

title: Choosing a taxi or prearranged ride
plain_summary: Use licensed taxis, official airport taxis or recognized booking apps. Ask for a vehicle with seatbelts; unlicensed services remain common. Confirm the destination and fare arrangement before departure.

title: Medical insurance and evacuation cover

title: Finding and paying for medical care
plain_summary: Care can be poorly equipped, especially outside major centers, and specialist cases may require treatment abroad. Arrange evacuation insurance and use insurer guidance for suitable facilities; do not assume advanced care is locally available.

title: Prescription preparation and import checks
plain_summary: Check the specific medicines against Uzbek customs rules before packing, including controlled ingredients and documentation. Bring permitted supplies with supporting prescriptions; legal status can differ from the United States.

title: Local SIM or eSIM setup
plain_summary: Ucell offers app-based SIM/eSIM registration for foreign visitors using a valid passport. Physical SIM registration still needs a starter pack; eSIM needs a compatible device. Follow identification and activation instructions and check coverage on your route.

sources.title: Ucell

title: Register the place where you stay
plain_summary: The government portal requires place-of-stay registration within three working days, with stated exemptions for transit/very short stays. Hotels handle registration automatically. Confirm completion with the property; after moving, check re-registration at the new address.

sources.title: Uzbekistan for foreigners

title: Airport terminal services and onward planning
plain_summary: Uzbekistan Airports’ terminal rules list information desks, exchange points, medical points and wireless internet zones. Check the actual arrival airport’s signs and service availability and prepare your accommodation and onward transport details before leaving the terminal.

title: Uzbek railway tickets and passport matching
plain_summary: Uzbek Railways issues nonresident electronic tickets using the passport intended for travel. Enter the details accurately, carry that passport and follow the official ticket/boarding instructions. Check the exact station, departure and cancellation conditions; high-speed and other train services are not interchangeable.
